quantities: Node extents use nodes, edge extents use edges, and emitted Relation occurrences use rows. Every dependency retains its actual input occurrence, producer and quantity. A conversion between quantities is justified only by the selected rule, never by matching numeric values.
construction: With an explicit node Relation, node count is bounded by its rows and edge count by the edge Relation's rows. Without it, at most two endpoint nodes are created per edge row, so node count is bounded by twice edge rows and edge count by edge rows. Identity deduplication does not increase either bound. Endpoint and property validation remain required.
combination: Union and two-input structural combination may use the sum of the respective input node bounds and the sum of the respective edge bounds. Retain repeated input occurrences even when their producer or proof CID is the same. Subtraction may use the left bounds alone. These conservative bounds do not assert that intersections emit every input entity or discharge identity conflict checks.
preservation: Normalization and subgraph selection do not increase node or edge counts and may retain the corresponding input bounds. This does not authorize preserving counts through arbitrary Graph-producing operations such as union or applying a Delta.
projection: node_rows and degree emit at most the input node count in rows; edge_rows emits at most the edge count. Node matching emits at most the original node count and edge matching at most the original edge count, regardless of repeated authored selectors. Components retains its input node extent for internal work and bounds its component rows by that extent.
selectors: A single endpoint has bound one. Explicit ID selectors use their admitted ID count. A Relation selector uses its corresponding Relation row bound; a node predicate uses the selected graph's node bound. These are conditional extents, not proofs of selector membership or uniqueness. Repeated Relation selector edges remain separate occurrences; sharing the graph node bound does not change their ownership.
traverse_nodes: For node emission, a graph node bound N and start extent S give at most min(S, N) * N rows. The clamp is justified by successful distinct graph-node start selection and one minimum eligible simple-path depth per start/end pair, after all hop and predicate conditions. It is applied before multiplication. This is not a path-emission bound; path multiplicity requires a separate finite bound and enforcement.
shortest_path: each_pair emits at most S * T rows for source and target extents. nearest_per_source emits at most S rows and does not need a target extent for this bound. nearest_pair emits at most one row and needs no endpoint count proof for that bound. These are upper bounds, including when no path exists, not assertions of nonempty output or successful endpoint admission.
arithmetic: Use exact nonnegative safe-integer arithmetic and reject addition or multiplication overflow. Do not round, saturate or replace unknown extents with zero. Select applicable clamps and operation-specific rules before arithmetic that the rule does not require.
conditionality: All derived bounds are conditional on operation success and retain validation dependencies. They do not establish observed input sizes, graph completeness, search-work or byte ceilings, authority, or completed resource enforcement. A failed check exposes no partial successful output.
